title: Sprint 1 — Git Fundamentals
description: Learn Git identity setup, committing, history exploration, and working with remote repositories.

tickets.title: Ticket 1 — Getting Started with Git
tickets.description:
Configure Git identity.
Initialize a repo and make your first commit.
Write a .gitignore for a Node.js project.

tasks.title: Task 1.1.1 — Configure Git Identity
tasks.description: Open the in-browser terminal and configure your global Git username and email address. Setting your identity is essential so that your commits are correctly attributed to you.

scoring_rules.pass_message: ✓ Git identity configured (user.name and user.email set).
scoring_rules.fail_hint: Run: git config --global user.name "Your Name" && git config --global user.email "you@example.com"

tasks.title: Task 1.1.2 — Initialize a Repo & First Commit
tasks.description: It's time to create your first repository! Initialize a new Git repository in the provided terminal. Create a new file, stage it, and make your first commit. Ensure your commit message is descriptive and at least 5 words long—avoid generic messages like 'first commit'.

checks.label: Stage a file with git add

scoring_rules.pass_message: ✓ Repository initialized, file staged, and committed.
scoring_rules.fail_hint: Run: git init && git add <file> && git commit -m "Descriptive commit message here"

tasks.title: Task 1.1.3 — Write a .gitignore for a Node.js Project
tasks.description: In the pre-seeded Node.js project, you'll find some files and directories that shouldn't be tracked by Git, such as dependencies, environment variables, build outputs, and logs. Create a configuration file to ignore these specific patterns (like node_modules, .env, dist, and log files). Verify that they no longer appear as untracked files, and make sure to commit your ignore file.

scoring_rules.pass_message: ✓ .gitignore created with node_modules & .env patterns, and committed.
scoring_rules.fail_hint: Create .gitignore with node_modules/ and .env lines, then: git add .gitignore && git commit -m "Add .gitignore"

tickets.title: Ticket 2 — Staging & Committing
tickets.description:
Practice partial staging with git add -p.
Amend a commit message.
Use git stash.

tasks.title: Task 1.2.1 — Partial Staging with git add -p
tasks.description: You have a file with multiple changes mixed together, but you only want to commit some of them right now. Interactively stage only two out of the three sections of changes in the file, and commit them. Leave the remaining section unstaged.

scoring_rules.pass_message: ✓ Used interactive partial staging (git add -p) and committed.
scoring_rules.fail_hint: Run: git add -p   (press 'y' to stage, 'n' to skip each hunk), then: git commit -m "message"

tasks.title: Task 1.2.2 — Amend a Commit Message
tasks.description: Oops! The last commit message in this repository was simply saved as a work-in-progress, which isn't very helpful. Modify the most recent commit message to be descriptive and at least 5 words long, without creating a brand new commit.

scoring_rules.pass_message: ✓ Commit message amended with git commit --amend.
scoring_rules.fail_hint: Run: git commit --amend -m "New descriptive message at least five words long"

tasks.title: Task 1.2.3 — Use git stash
tasks.description: You have some uncommitted changes, but you need to switch contexts to work on something else quickly. Temporarily set aside your current changes, make a small separate commit, and then restore your set-aside changes so you can continue working on them.

checks.label: Restore stash with git stash pop or apply

scoring_rules.pass_message: ✓ Used git stash, made a separate commit, and restored stash.
scoring_rules.fail_hint: Run: git stash  ->  make commit  ->  git stash pop

tickets.title: Ticket 3 — Viewing History
tickets.description:
Explore git log flags.
Use git diff.
Bug hunt with git bisect.

tasks.title: Task 1.3.1 — Explore git log Flags
tasks.description: Let's explore the history of this repository. It has multiple commits, authors, and branches. Use the history command with different flags to view a condensed one-line summary, visualize the branch graph for all branches, and filter the commits to show only those by a specific author.

scoring_rules.pass_message: ✓ Used git log with --oneline, --graph, and --author flags.
scoring_rules.fail_hint:
Run:
  git log --oneline
  git log --graph --all --oneline
  git log --author="Your Name"

tasks.title: Task 1.3.2 — Use git diff
tasks.description: You have both staged and unstaged changes in your workspace. Inspect the differences to see exactly what has changed. View the diff for your unstaged modifications, and then separately view the diff for the changes you have already staged for commit.

checks.label: Diff unstaged changes with git diff
Diff staged changes with git diff --staged or --cached

scoring_rules.pass_message: ✓ Used git diff for unstaged and git diff --staged for staged changes.
scoring_rules.fail_hint: Run: git diff   (unstaged) and then: git diff --staged   (staged)

tasks.title: Task 1.3.3 — Bug Hunt with git bisect
tasks.description: A bug was introduced somewhere in the last 15 commits. Clone the provided repository locally and use Git's binary search tool to find the exact commit that caused the issue. Once you identify the bad commit, create a file named BISECT_RESULT.txt containing only that commit's hash and push it to the repository.

scoring_rules.pass_message: ✓ Used git bisect correctly to find the buggy commit.
scoring_rules.fail_hint: Run: git bisect start  ->  git bisect bad  ->  git bisect good <known-good-hash>

tickets.title: Ticket 4 — Remote Repositories
tickets.description:
Push a local repo to GitHub.
Clone, change, and push.
Set up SSH key authentication.

tasks.title: Task 1.4.1 — Push Local Repo to GitHub
tasks.description: Now that you have a local repository with some history, it's time to share it. Create a new remote repository on GitHub using the provided naming convention, and push your local repository and its commits to this new remote destination. Ensure your default branch is set correctly.

scoring_rules.pass_message: ✓ Remote added and repository pushed to GitHub.
scoring_rules.fail_hint: Run: git remote add origin <url> && git push -u origin main

tasks.title: Task 1.4.2 — Clone → Change → Push
tasks.description: You've been provided with a starter GitHub repository. Clone it to your local machine, create a new feature branch, and add a meaningful section to the README. Once you're done, push your feature branch to the remote repository. Remember not to push directly to the main branch!

scoring_rules.pass_message: ✓ Cloned repo, created feature branch, and pushed to remote.
scoring_rules.fail_hint: Run: git clone <url>  ->  git checkout -b feature/<name>  ->  git push origin <branch>

tasks.title: Task 1.4.3 — SSH Key Authentication
tasks.description: Secure your connection to GitHub by setting up SSH authentication. Generate a new SSH key pair and add the public key to your GitHub account settings. For bonus points, verify your setup by cloning a repository using its SSH URL instead of HTTPS.

checks.label: Verify SSH connection or add key to agent

scoring_rules.pass_message: ✓ SSH key generated and verified with GitHub.
scoring_rules.fail_hint: Run: ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "you@email.com"  then add public key to GitHub and test: ssh -T git@github.com
